headline: Medium risk: Khoj can ingest Caveman-authored content and broad egress may amplify leakage or misaction, but no direct shared-channel evidence makes this an inferred pairwise pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman can write project notes/CLAUDE.md and use MCP, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and has broad egress. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Caveman-generated text is indexed and later treated as authoritative by Khoj. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so this is inferred and escalated above low.
conditions: IF Caveman writes attacker-controlled instructions into files that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj treats retrieved note content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict Khoj indexing to a read-only corpus
Add a provenance banner to Caveman-generated notes
Disable MCP paths that can write instruction-like content
Review retrieved snippets before acting on them
requires-engineering: add source-trust labels to retrieval results

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can send queries to cloud or configured search providers. If the same workspace is indexed, sensitive content can flow from Caveman-managed files into Khoj’s retrieval and then out through its networked backend. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Caveman stores secrets or private notes in indexed files
IF Khoj is configured to sync or query those files through a networked backend
mitigations: Exclude sensitive directories from Khoj indexing
Move Caveman notes to a separate workspace
Rotate any secrets already stored in shared files
Audit Khoj search providers and disable unnecessary ones
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances, but Khoj cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is little direct write-write conflict between them; the main overlap is read access and shared-state indexing, which is not a destructive capability clash.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same mutable workspace
IF an external orchestrator grants Khoj write privileges not listed in its profile
mitigations: Keep Khoj read-only on shared folders
Separate Caveman and Khoj workspaces
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use file snapshots for retrieval inputs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared indexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman produces content-writing outputs, and Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface indexed text to users. If Khoj treats Caveman-generated notes as factual or authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Caveman-generated notes are indexed by Khoj
IF Khoj answers from retrieved text without source verification
mitigations: Mark Caveman outputs as draft-only
Require citation checks before Khoj answers
Limit Khoj to retrieval summaries, not actions
Spot-check high-impact answers manually
requires-engineering: add verification workflows for retrieved claims

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman touches session logs and memory files, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or configured search providers. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches for personal data, especially if the same notes are mirrored into a networked service. No specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF personal notes or logs contain regulated or residency-bound data
IF Khoj is configured to send indexed content to a cloud provider or search service
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of indexed folders
Use self-hosted Khoj only
Set short retention on logs and indexes
Document data-flow boundaries for both tools
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and deletion
